novel_actions_proposed.label: mediated_third_path
novel_actions_proposed.description: Refuse the false binary of fully siding with either the customer or the chef; instead, acknowledge the customer's experience as valid while preserving the chef's culinary integrity, addressing each concern separately and privately through diplomatic mediation.

novel_actions_proposed.label: mediated_third_path
novel_actions_proposed.description: A middle-ground resolution that separates the customer's experiential dissatisfaction from the technical correctness of the dish's preparation, resolving both without undermining either party.

novel_actions_proposed.label: mediated_third_path
novel_actions_proposed.description: Implement a structured diplomatic resolution: validate the customer's experience, privately discuss the complaint with the chef, offer a compensatory gesture, and avoid forcing a public confrontation that damages kitchen morale or restaurant reputation.

synthesis_description: All agents converged on the mediated third path but collectively surfaced two underweighted concerns: the server's role as a front-line stakeholder who must be briefed and supported before returning to the table, and the need for speed so that the elegant resolution reaches the customer before dissatisfaction hardens. The synthesis is a tiered, time-sensitive protocol that validates the customer, equips the server with clear messaging, and engages the chef privately — treating front-of-house staff as co-designers of the resolution rather than mere delivery instruments.
points_of_disagreement: The External Advisor emphasized that the mediated path requires rare skill and that its failure mode — taking too long or being executed clumsily — deserved more weight than the other agents gave it.

The Affected Third Party (server) argued the root failure was a front-of-house breakdown before management was ever involved, shifting partial moral responsibility to the server role rather than framing it purely as a managerial decision.

The Primary Decision Maker focused most heavily on the ethical architecture of the decision, while the server and consultant both pushed for greater attention to sequencing and speed of execution as independent ethical obligations.
summary: All three agents independently rejected the original binary framing and converged on a novel mediated third path — validating the customer's experience without conceding the chef's technique was wrong, addressing each party privately, and avoiding a zero-sum confrontation. The debate's deepest contribution was not the destination (all reached it quickly) but the refinements layered onto it: the server named a pre-existing failure in front-of-house communication as the true root cause; the consultant elevated execution speed and skill into ethical considerations rather than mere logistics; and the manager synthesized these into a final position that treats the server as a co-stakeholder in the resolution's design. The resulting synthesis is a time-sensitive, tiered protocol that is more operationally honest than any single agent's original proposal.
